takeaway: Cardiac index = cardiac output / body surface area. Reference range 2.5–4 L/min/m².

lines.text: This equation takes the heart's output and scales it to the size of the patient's body.
and divide it by the body surface area.
That gives the output per square metre of body surface.
The result is the cardiac index.
Its reference range is 2.5 to 4 L/min/m².
lines.say: Its reference range is two point five to four litres per minute per square metre.

lines.text: So: cardiac index equals cardiac output divided by body surface area.
